analysis:
Examined the added paged-session source, the complete plan patch/source and file metadata, plus the bounded Prefix.swift excerpt. No independently supported security regression was identified in this scope. Gemma4TensorParallelPagedSession.swift:64–90 checks request capacity and prefix geometry before adopting into fresh request state; :118–143 checks prefill frontiers, :150–202 validates decode tokens and distinct batch sessions, and :212–219,304–309 retires state and checks drainage. Plan.swift:103–203 restricts model configuration, quantization and head/channel splits; :291–343 rejects unknown tensor keys and invalid ranks, and :396–430 checks cut shapes/alignment. These controls concern TB-007, A-001/A-004 and T-007/T-027/T-028; shape validation is not proof of correct computation or memory erasure.
Integration must trace supplied callers and dependencies: prefix adoption/capture must bind model, rank and authenticated tenant scope (T-041), and cancellation/authorization checks must reach state.run/runBatch and final response delivery (T-010/T-053). The public oracle generation path at PagedSession.swift:265–298 supplies only MLX error checks; its production reachability is not established, so this is not evidence of bypassing serving cancellation or authorization.
The Prefix.swift excerpt at lines 6–28 describes resident RAM plus optional encrypted SSD caching and two-rank offer/confirm coordination. Compare actual construction, tenant partitioning, persistent scope and retention with T-041's production SSD-only posture. Comments alone do not establish production activation or a weakened cache gate. Prefix.swift's remaining source, cache implementations and caller wiring are outside this batch; these are material integration questions, not findings. No changes to token custody, attestation, response encryption, billing or privileged helper controls are demonstrated by these units.
